title: Interest, Loans and Pledges
lead: Israel's law forbids charging interest to a fellow Israelite in need, limits what a lender may take as a pledge, and cancels debts every seventh year (Exodus 22:25–27; Leviticus 25:35–37; Deuteronomy 15:1–11; 23:19–20; 24:6–13). Jewish and Christian thinkers have argued for centuries over how these laws apply to business lending.
